title: How to Connect GitHub to Slack (Official App + Alternatives)
description: GitHub's official Slack app, subscription commands, and webhook-based alternatives for repo and PR notifications.
bodyHtml:
Getting pull request, issue, and deployment activity into Slack is one of the most common integrations for engineering teams, and GitHub ships an official app for it, so most teams don't need a third-party tool for the basics.

MethodSetup effortBest for
Official GitHub app for SlackLowStandard PR/issue/release notifications
Zapier / MakeMediumFiltering by label, author, or custom formatting
Webhooks (custom)HighFull control over payload, routing to multiple channels by rule

Method 1: The official GitHub Slack app

Install "GitHub" from the Slack App Directory, authenticate, then subscribe a channel to a repo:

/github subscribe owner/repo
/github subscribe owner/repo issues, pulls, releases

You can scope which event types post (issues, pulls, commits, deployments, releases) per channel, and the app also unfurls links to PRs and issues pasted into Slack with live status. This covers most teams' needs with zero code.

Method 2: Zapier or Make

Useful when you want conditional routing the native app doesn't support, e.g. only post PRs labeled "needs-review" to a specific channel, or post a summary message rather than GitHub's default formatting:

  • Trigger: "New Pull Request" or "New Issue" in GitHub
  • Filter: label contains a specific value
  • Action: "Send Channel Message" in Slack, with a custom template

Method 3: Raw GitHub webhooks (for developers)

For full control, configure a webhook on the repo (Settings → Webhooks) pointing at a small server or serverless function that receives GitHub's event payload, applies whatever routing/filtering logic you need, and posts to Slack via a Bot token or Incoming Webhook. This is the only option that supports arbitrary logic, like routing by CODEOWNERS, or fan-out to multiple channels based on the changed file paths.

Which to pick

Start with the official app; it covers the standard notification use case without any setup cost. Move to Zapier/Make for filtering, and only build custom webhook handling once you need routing logic tied to your repo's specific conventions.
